hints.title: Pairwise Concatenation Ordering
hints.text: When deciding whether string representation a should precede string representation b, comparing concatenation a plus b against b plus a establishes total ordering.

hints.title: Transitive Total Order Invariant
hints.text: If a plus b is lexicographically greater than b plus a, then a must appear before b in the optimal sequence to maximize the combined value.

hints.title: Custom Comparator Sort Procedure
hints.text: Convert all integers to strings. Sort strings using a custom comparator where a precedes b if a plus b exceeds b plus a. Join the sorted strings. If the first character is zero, return string zero to prevent multiple leading zeros.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def largestNumber(self, nums: List[int]) -> str:
        from functools import cmp_to_key
        strs = [str(x) for x in nums]
        strs.sort(key=cmp_to_key(lambda a, b: 1 if a + b < b + a else -1))
        res = "".join(strs)
        return "0" if res[0] == "0" else res
```

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N log N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all N! permutations takes factorial time and immediately exhausts execution limits.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting strings with the custom pairwise concatenation comparator takes O(N log N * K) time where K is max string length, with O(N) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should prove transitivity of the concatenation comparator and remember to handle the all-zeros corner case.
